templates.name: Platformer
templates.description: The smallest working platform game, on Kenney's Pixel Platformer art: a player that runs and jumps, ground to stand on, a ledge to drop through, a wall to slide down and jump off, and a camera that follows.

demos.name: Platformer demo
demos.description: A small complete platform game on Kenney's Pixel Platformer art: coins, slimes to squash, spikes, a flag and a saved best.

demos.name: Rocky demo
demos.description: A platform level in a cave on Szadi art's Rocky Level art: diamonds and hearts, slimes to stomp, bats, a snapping plant, crystals, three hearts and a saved best, with lights that glow on the crystals and drift past the ledges, their shadows moving.

demos.name: Two players demo
demos.description: The Platformer demo for two on one keyboard, or a keyboard and a pad: each player has their own control set and half of the screen, and one Player Type with one set of rules serves both.

demos.name: Online demo
demos.description: The Two players demo played online, the way an online game usually goes: a title screen to host a game, play online or join by code; a waiting room with names, Ready, an invite link and the host's Start; then the level, each game moving its own player while the other's follows.

demos.name: Dungeon demo
demos.description: Six rooms seen from above on Kenney's Tiny Dungeon art: bats that chase, spiders and rats on patrol, arrows, a dark room lit by a lantern, a key, a locked door and a chest. Each room is its own scene, changed by a Scene Manager in a singleton that keeps the player and the HUD.

demos.name: Physics demo
demos.description: A playground on the Box2D solver: a rope bridge of hinged planks, a car on wheel joints that picks up crates, a wrecking ball, a see-saw, a pool that floats what falls in, a fan, and everything draggable with the mouse.

demos.name: Cascade demo
demos.description: Water and shapes down a flight of ramps and conveyor belts on the Box2D solver and the Fluid behavior: discs, squares, triangles and pentagons drop in with a random gravity scale, the belts carry them by their surface speed, a drain takes the water, and every contact point is drawn. Click to splash, drag to stir; with Space held the left button makes water, with D it takes water away.

demos.name: Tank demo
demos.description: Water and crates on the arcade solver: the Fluid poured along flat shelves over a weir into a sink, carrying and floating arcade Physics Bodies. The cascade demo's idea on the other solver.

demos.name: Particles demo
demos.description: Water, sand and sparks on the Fluid behavior, and a scene for each of its kinds: a deep pool in passes, a pool that sleeps, elastic jelly, a spring net, walls made of particles, oil and water that repel, color mixing, color by speed, and objects turned into particles. Keys 1 to 0 change scene.

demos.name: BunnyMark
demos.description: How many moving pictures before the frame rate drops: bouncing bunnies each moved by its own visual script, and trees of slowly turning bunnies. Hold the left button to add ten a frame, the right to take ten away.

demos.name: Noise world
demos.description: A native C library in a game: stb_perlin's noise grows an island on a tile map, drifts clouds over it and steers a boat, through a behavior that offers its numbers to rules. Built on the first Run with your C++ compiler.

demos.name: Particle effects demo
demos.description: A scene for each thing a Particles object does: a campfire on color gradients and curves, rain and snow that collide, sparks whose hits pick the crates they land on, magic carried with a wand or left behind, animated rings, a geyser on a rate curve and fireworks on a click. Keys 1 to 6 change scene.

demos.name: Menus demo
demos.description: A title screen, an options screen with a volume slider and a rebind table, and a small game with a pause menu: every screen built from the engine's own UI objects under a screen-fixed layer, walked by Tab, the arrows or a pad, and driven by rules.

demos.name: Dialogue demo
demos.description: A conversation with a gate guard written in a Yarn file and shown by rules in a box of the engine's own UI objects: a portrait, the speaker, the line and a button per choice; commands change the portrait and hand over gold, and the guard remembers whether you have talked before.

demos.name: Skeletons demo
demos.description: Four characters, each showing off what bones do: a dinosaur that walks and runs (rigid legs, a body and tail that bend as meshes), a tree swaying on a motor with jiggling leaf clumps, a jellyfish pulsing by deform keys with waving tentacles, and a dapper skeleton that tips its hat and dances the Charleston. Hold the mouse on one to change what it does; hold B to see the bones.
